title: DbfRow.Fields is a non-concurrent Dictionary<string,object?> — 10 parallel WriteField calls on the same client race on the same row
impact: Two concurrent WriteField calls on the SAME ClientNumber (different fields, different idempotency keys) execute in parallel because the per-key SemaphoreSlim serializes by key, not by row. Both end up at `row.Fields[field] = value` on a plain Dictionary, which can corrupt the internal bucket array (lost write, InvalidOperationException, or in the worst case an infinite loop inside Dictionary.Insert). A concurrent ListClients/ReadClient/CloneRow enumerating Fields can throw 'Collection was modified' mid-iteration, surfacing as a generic InternalServerError to the operator.
description: DbfRow declares `public Dictionary<string, object?> Fields { get; init; }`. Both write paths — LacerteSessionManager.ApplySimFieldWriteWithUndo line 1725 (`row.Fields[field] = value`) and SimulationStore.SimulateFieldWrite line 344 — mutate this dict with NO lock. The P14-005 per-key SemaphoreSlim in ExecuteWithIdempotencyLock only serializes calls sharing the SAME idempotencyKey; with 10 parallel WriteField calls carrying 10 distinct keys but all targeting client 1001 fields C1_15, C1_27, C1_29, ..., they all reach the unlocked assignment simultaneously. ReadClient/ListClients on the same client call CloneRow which iterates `src.Fields` (line 1884 `foreach (var kv in src.Fields)`) without locking either — guaranteed to throw under load. The existing P14-028 lock(list) fix for DetailRow lists shows the project knows the per-row data structures need locks; the DbfRow.Fields dict was missed.
recommendation: Either (a) change DbfRow.Fields to ConcurrentDictionary<string, object?>, or (b) add `lock (row.Fields)` around every mutation site (ApplySimFieldWriteWithUndo line 1725, SimulateFieldWrite line 344) AND every enumeration site (CloneRow line 1884, ListClients filter at 734, every other foreach over Fields). Option (a) is cheaper to land — the only contract change is that init-time bulk assignment in SimulateCreateClient (line 549-557 initializer) needs to use Add or indexer. Add a SimulationStoreConcurrencyTests sibling that pounds WriteField on the same client from 16 threads with 16 distinct fields + reads from 8 more threads — without the fix the test will throw InvalidOperationException or lose writes within a few hundred iterations.
rationale: Prior P14-028 work added lock(list) to per-client detail-row lists and the existing SimulationStoreConcurrencyTests prove the team thinks about this hazard — but the DbfRow.Fields dict (used for DATA1-5 row writes, the bulk of WriteField traffic) was never converted. A tax pro batching 10 fields onto one client via 10 parallel tool calls — exactly what an LLM does when prompted 'fill in the taxpayer info' — hits this race on the very first session.

verdict.reasoning:
VERIFIED REAL. SimulationStore.cs line 38 declares `public Dictionary<string, object?> Fields { get; init; } = new Dictionary<string, object?>();` — confirmed plain Dictionary, not ConcurrentDictionary. Two write sites mutate it without locks: (1) SimulationStore.cs line 344 `row.Fields[field] = value` inside SimulateFieldWrite, and (2) LacerteSessionManager.cs line 1725 (plus line 1717-1721 inside the undo closure) inside ApplySimFieldWriteWithUndo. Multiple enumeration sites are unlocked too: CloneRow at LacerteSessionManager.cs line 1884 (`foreach (var kv in src.Fields)`), SimulationStore.cs line 681 (Snapshot clone), and SimulationStore.cs line 534 (`existing.Fields.TryGetValue("ClientID", ...)` during duplicate-ClientID scan inside SimulateCreateClient — a CreateClient concurrent with a WriteField on any client races on this enumeration).

VERIFIED P14-005 SCOPE GAP. ExecuteWithIdempotencyLock at LacerteSessionManager.cs lines 1931-1948 calls `_idempotencyLocks.GetOrAdd(key, _ => new SemaphoreSlim(1, 1))` — the semaphore is keyed by `idempotencyKey`, NOT by (clientNumber, table). Two parallel WriteField calls with distinct idempotency keys but the same client/table never share a semaphore. The finding's claim that "10 parallel WriteField calls carrying 10 distinct keys but all targeting client 1001 fields" reach `row.Fields[field] = value` simultaneously is correct. Even more damning: if no idempotency key is supplied at all (lines 1934-1937 short-circuit), there is zero serialization.

VERIFIED P14-028 DIFFERENT SCOPE. P14-028 added `lock (list)` to the per-client `List<DetailRow>` lists in SimulationStore.WriteDetail/ReadDetail and to ApplySimDetailWrite (LacerteSessionManager.cs line 1749). SimulationStoreConcurrencyTests is explicitly scoped to "P14-028 — SimulationStore.WriteDetail and ReadDetail" (file comment lines 11-12). It pounds DetailRow lists, never DbfRow.Fields. The finding's observation that "the existing P14-028 lock(list) fix... shows the project knows the per-row data structures need locks; the DbfRow.Fields dict was missed" is exactly right.

VERIFIED NOVEL. Grepped all four audit-findings*.json files for DbfRow, Fields, row.Fields, ApplySimFieldWrite, SimulateFieldWrite, CloneRow, Collection.modified, InvalidOperationException, concurrent.Dictionary, Dictionary.race. Findings touching adjacent territory:
- P14-005 (r1): per-key idempotency semaphore — keyed by idempotencyKey not row, does NOT cover this race
- P14-028 (r1): lock(list) for DetailRow lists — different data structure
- P14-030 (r1): ApplySimCreateClient bypass of SimulateCreateClient gates — correctness divergence, not concurrency
- P14-070, P17-011 (r4): CloneRow casing/clone shape — discuss what CloneRow emits, never that its `foreach (var kv in src.Fields)` enumeration is unlocked
- audit-findings.json:304 — references CloneRow only for pagination cost
None of the 251 prior findings address DbfRow.Fields as a concurrent-mutation hazard.

MATERIALLY IMPROVES. .NET Dictionary<TKey,TValue> is documented as not thread-safe; concurrent writes can corrupt the bucket array (in worst-case .NET 4.8 a corrupted Dictionary can spin forever inside Insert). The finding's worst-case scenarios (lost write, InvalidOperationException from enumeration, "Collection was modified" mid-iterate) are all reachable. The realistic operator scenario — LLM batching "fill in taxpayer info" into multiple parallel WriteField tool calls on the same client — is exactly the access pattern. The fix is small (convert one property type OR add lock at ~6 sites) and the seed-data dict initializer at line 549-557 is the only contract change needed for option (a). SimulationStoreConcurrencyTests already exists as a test pattern to extend.

CAVEAT (downgraded severity but not finding validity): stdio MCP requests are often serialized by the host, and this is a single-operator personal tool (CLAUDE.md frames it as "Personal tool. Bar is 'works flawlessly,' not 'ships to customers.'"). So the real-world hit probability is moderate, not certain. But the finding stands because (a) MCP host serialization is not guaranteed by spec, (b) Claude/LLM hosts can and do invoke multiple tool calls in parallel, (c) the fix-vs-cost ratio is excellent (small structural change, off-Windows verifiable, existing test pattern to extend), and (d) the project has explicitly invested in concurrency hardening (P14-005, P14-028) — leaving DbfRow.Fields as the only remaining unguarded core data structure is inconsistent with that investment.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Land as a P17-018 (or next P-id) sibling of P14-028. Sim-only, off-Windows actionable, ~30 LOC code + ~60 LOC test. Prefer option (a) ConcurrentDictionary over option (b) lock-everywhere because (i) it's structurally self-enforcing — future code that adds a new enumeration site doesn't need to remember to lock, (ii) it eliminates the risk of deadlock if a future caller already holds the ModuleStore concurrent map's internal locks, and (iii) ConcurrentDictionary's TryGetValue is lock-free, so the hot ReadField path stays fast.

1. SimulationStore.cs line 38 — change `public Dictionary<string, object?> Fields { get; init; } = new Dictionary<string, object?>();` to `public ConcurrentDictionary<string, object?> Fields { get; init; } = new ConcurrentDictionary<string, object?>();`.

2. SimulationStore.cs line 549-558 — the collection initializer `Fields = { ["C1_0"] = clientNumber, ... }` desugars to the indexer which ConcurrentDictionary supports as an upsert, so this should compile without change. VERIFY: `ConcurrentDictionary<TKey,TValue>` does expose the `this[TKey]` indexer with set semantics, so dictionary-initializer syntax with bracket assignments works. Run `dotnet build` to confirm.

3. SimulationStore.cs line 681 (Snapshot CloneRow) — `foreach (var kv in src.Fields) dst.Fields[kv.Key] = kv.Value;` is already concurrent-safe with ConcurrentDictionary (enumeration is a moment-in-time snapshot).

4. SimulationStore.Seed.cs lines 75, 91, 101-103, 146, 157, 162-164, 173, 189, 200, 205-207, 216 — same initializer pattern, all use bracket assignment, so all desugar to the indexer; no change needed but spot-check after the type change compiles.

5. LacerteSessionManager.cs line 1717-1725 — the undo closure does `row.Fields.TryGetValue` / `row.Fields[field] = value` / `row.Fields.Remove(field)`. ConcurrentDictionary supports all three but the Remove inside the undo should switch to `TryRemove(field, out _)` (the non-generic `Remove(TKey)` method returns void on ConcurrentDictionary via the IDictionary interface; cleaner to be explicit). Note: the TryGetValue → assign sequence inside this undo is now subject to lost-update if two undos race on the same field, but undos only run inside dry-run rollback which is single-threaded per request, so this is fine.

6. LacerteSessionManager.cs line 1884 (CloneRow for wire emission) — enumeration becomes naturally safe.

7. ConcurrentDictionary changes IEnumerable order semantics slightly compared to Dictionary (no insertion-order guarantee in .NET 4.8 for either, but ConcurrentDictionary is even less predictable). Check tests that snapshot row.Fields enumeration order — most likely none rely on order, but worth a `dotnet test` pass to confirm before landing.

8. Add `DbfRowFieldsConcurrencyTests` (sibling of SimulationStoreConcurrencyTests). Pattern:
   - Test A: 16 threads × 16 distinct fields × 250 writes each on the SAME ClientNumber via SimulationStore.SimulateFieldWrite or LacerteSessionManager.WriteFieldAsync. Assert no exception thrown, final state has all 16 fields with their last-written value. Without the fix, the test will throw InvalidOperationException or lose writes within a few hundred iterations.
   - Test B: 8 writer threads + 8 reader threads (ReadClient or ListClients) on the same client. Without the fix, the readers enumerate during a backing-bucket reallocation and throw "Collection was modified" / NullRef. With ConcurrentDictionary, no exception.
   - Test C: 4 threads calling SimulateCreateClient (which scans `store.Clients.Values` checking `existing.Fields.TryGetValue("ClientID", ...)` at line 534-541) + 4 threads writing fields on existing clients. Asserts the duplicate-scan enumeration never throws.

9. Add a one-line comment near the new ConcurrentDictionary declaration explaining the rationale and pointing at P14-028's sibling rationale, so future contributors don't "simplify" it back to Dictionary.

10. Update DECISIONS.md with a brief entry alongside P14-028's "per-client list lock" entry: "DbfRow.Fields uses ConcurrentDictionary because LLM-driven tool batching can write distinct fields on the same client concurrently; the per-key idempotency semaphore (P14-005) only serializes same-key calls, so distinct-key concurrent writes were unguarded prior to this change."

Sequence after Stage 4 idempotency lock work: this and P14-005 / P14-028 form a triad — verify all three remain consistent. Specifically, do NOT also add a redundant `lock (row.Fields)` on top of ConcurrentDictionary — `lock` on a ConcurrentDictionary instance works but is a code smell that suggests the lock is doing real work, when in fact it's belt-and-suspenders.

Severity calibration: the finding's "high" is defensible for the data-corruption potential (Dictionary corruption in .NET 4.8 has documented infinite-loop pathologies), but for a single-operator personal tool with stdio transport, "medium" is more honest. Land at medium severity in the changelog; the fix is worth doing regardless.

title: Dry-run CreateClient's undo unconditionally Exchanges NextClientNumber back to a stale snapshot — concurrent real CreateClient can mint a duplicate ClientNumber
impact: Sequence: Thread A starts a dry-run CreateClient, captures priorNext=1001, increments to 1002, returns. Before A's finally runs the undo, Thread B starts a REAL CreateClient, increments to 1003, mints ClientNumber='1002' (Increment-then-subtract-1). Thread A's undo then Interlocked.Exchanges NextClientNumber back to 1001. Thread C starts a real CreateClient, mints ClientNumber='1001' — but wait, 1002 was already given to B. Thread D then mints '1002' again — DUPLICATE ClientNumber colliding with B's row in store.Clients (since `store.Clients[clientNumber] = row` simply overwrites). Two clients with different operator-supplied ClientId but the same minted ClientNumber, one silently overwritten. Tax data loss.
description: Line 1820: `var priorNext = module?.NextClientNumber ?? 0;` captures a non-volatile read. Line 1822 calls SimulateCreateClient which on success increments NextClientNumber atomically at SimulationStore.cs:546. Line 1842: `Interlocked.Exchange(ref capturedModule.NextClientNumber, capturedPriorNext);` rolls the counter back unconditionally. The Exchange is atomic but the LOGIC is wrong — it assumes no concurrent CreateClient incremented in between, which is not enforced anywhere. CreateClient does NOT take the per-key SemaphoreSlim (idempotencyKey is OPTIONAL — when null, ExecuteWithIdempotencyLock at line 1934 bypasses locking entirely), so two concurrent CreateClient calls with no idempotency key run wide-open. The dry-run snapshot at line 580 of SimulationStore is the legacy whole-store approach; P14-043 replaced it with per-op undos that work in single-threaded but break under concurrent dry-run + real-create.
recommendation: Replace the unconditional Exchange with a CompareExchange that ONLY rolls back if NextClientNumber is still capturedPriorNext+1 (proving no one else incremented). If not, leave the counter where the parallel creators put it — the dry-run's allocated number is effectively 'leaked' but no collision occurs: `Interlocked.CompareExchange(ref capturedModule.NextClientNumber, capturedPriorNext, capturedPriorNext + 1);`. Add a concurrency test that runs 32 parallel mix of dry-run + real CreateClient and asserts every Clients.Keys entry is unique AND every emitted ClientNumber is unique — without the fix, expect O(threads^2/N) duplicate-ClientNumber events on contended runs.
rationale: P14-043 removed the whole-module snapshot in favor of per-op undos for performance, and the prior audits never composed the new undo with parallel CreateClient — every prior round examined undo in isolation. The duplicate ClientNumber outcome is silent (Dictionary indexer overwrite, not throw) and tax-data-destroying, which is the worst severity profile for the operator's actual use case.

verdict.reasoning:
VERIFIED REAL. Re-traced the race at C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/src/LacertMCP.Server/Session/LacerteSessionManager.cs:1808-1847 against SimulationStore.cs:546 (`Interlocked.Increment(ref store.NextClientNumber) - 1`) and the dry-run dispatch at 1470-1478 (`try { ApplySim...; } finally { undo?.Invoke(); }`).

The trace holds:
- Line 1820: `priorNext = module?.NextClientNumber ?? 0` is a plain non-volatile read of capturedPriorNext.
- Line 1822: SimulateCreateClient atomically increments NextClientNumber (priorNext -> priorNext+1) and mints clientNumber = priorNext.
- Line 1842: undo unconditionally `Interlocked.Exchange(ref capturedModule.NextClientNumber, capturedPriorNext)`.

Given CreateClient at line 1383 calls ExecuteWithIdempotencyLock which at 1934 BYPASSES the per-key semaphore when idempotencyKey is null/empty, two concurrent CreateClient calls (one dry-run, one real) with no idempotency key run with no serialization between the Increment in SimulateCreateClient and the Exchange in the undo closure. The window between A's Increment->1002 and A's Exchange->1001 can hold B's Increment->1003+mint("1002"). After A's Exchange, NextClientNumber=1001 while Clients["1002"] holds B's row. The next two real CreateClients then mint "1001" (safe) and "1002" (silently overwrites B's row via `store.Clients[clientNumber] = row` at SimulationStore.cs:559 — Dictionary indexer assignment, no throw).

The finding's core mechanism is correct.

VERIFIED NOVEL. Grep across all four prior round JSONs for {undo, NextClientNumber, CompareExchange, capturedPriorNext, ApplySimCreateClient, dry-run+concurrent}: P14-043 introduced the per-op undo specifically to replace the whole-module SimSnapshot (audit-findings.json:920-947); its verdict explicitly recommended the closure shape now in use, but verified the undo composition only in single-threaded reasoning ("CreateClient assigns a new ClientNumber → snapshot just NextClientNumber and remove the added Clients entry"). Neither P14-043's verdict nor any of P15/P16/P17 considered the dry-run-undo composing with a concurrent real CreateClient. P17-004 (audit-findings-r4.json:85+) covered idempotency cache cold-start (different surface). No prior finding addresses the unconditional-Exchange race or proposes the CompareExchange guard.

MATERIALLY IMPROVES — moderately. The race is real but practical likelihood is moderate: the operator profile (single tax pro driving Claude Desktop) typically issues sequential tool calls awaiting each result. However, the CSV bulk-intake prompt (lacerte_csv_intake) is exactly the workflow where an LLM may emit parallel tool calls, and modern hosts do support concurrent tool invocation. The failure mode is silent (Dictionary overwrite, no throw, no log) and lossy (tax data destroyed). The fix is a one-line CompareExchange and is correct: if NextClientNumber is still capturedPriorNext+1, roll back; otherwise leave it (numbers "leak" but no collision). Cheap, correct, and closes a silent-data-loss vector — meets the round-5 bar.

Mild dampener: the same lack-of-locking pattern means a duplicate-ClientID race exists even without dry-run (two concurrent real CreateClients with the same ClientId pass the duplicate-ID gate at SimulationStore.cs:534-541 concurrently before either mints — different bug, not what this finding addresses). The proposed fix doesn't close that one, but it's also not in scope.

One correction to the finding's recommendation: the recommended CompareExchange parameter order is `Interlocked.CompareExchange(ref NextClientNumber, capturedPriorNext, capturedPriorNext + 1)` — i.e., compare-to-(priorNext+1), swap-to-priorNext. That's what the finding wrote; verified the .NET signature is `CompareExchange(ref location, value, comparand)` so the spelling is right.

title: CSV intake prompt names DuplicateClient as 'status 18' — actual code is 12; status 18 is DB3Error
impact: An LLM following the lacerte_csv_intake prompt verbatim will (a) treat real DuplicateClient (statusCode 12) responses as some other error and may not STOP/skip-duplicates as instructed, AND (b) treat any DB3Error (statusCode 18 — a state DB I/O failure) as a duplicate-skip case. In a CSV bulk-intake with the 'skip duplicates' flag, a transient DB3Error would silently drop a row that should have been retried — the operator would never know a real client was lost from the import.
description: WorkflowPrompts.cs line 291 (CsvIntake Step 4) reads: `On 'DuplicateClient' (status 18) STOP unless the operator explicitly said 'skip duplicates'`. But StatusCodes.cs line 43 defines `DuplicateClient = 12` and line 49 defines `DB3Error = 18`. The integer in the prompt is wrong by 6. The prompt's same paragraph also tells the LLM to 'surface the structured userMessage + remediation' for any other non-Success code, so the LLM is being told to switch on a numeric code that does not exist for that name. The CsvIntake prompt is the canonical bulk-onboarding workflow per REQUIREMENTS §1.3, so this misroutes the highest-volume happy path on a real DuplicateClient and silently misclassifies any DB3Error as a duplicate.
recommendation: Edit WorkflowPrompts.cs line 291 to say `(status 12)` instead of `(status 18)`. Even better: drop the numeric and just reference the name (`On 'DuplicateClient' STOP unless...`) since the StatusCodes table is the source of truth and the prompt's own narrative tells the LLM to read `statusCode + statusName` from the structured error. Add a unit test in PromptsTests that scrapes the prompt body for `(status N)` patterns and asserts each maps to the correct named code via StatusCodes reflection — same defense as the cross-tool naming sweep.
rationale: Searched all 4 prior audit files for DuplicateClient / 'status 12' / 'status 18' / prompt-numeric-mismatch — the r4 P17-003/P17-004 DuplicateClient mentions are about idempotency cache cold-start, not prompt-vs-status-table integer drift. No prior round walked the prompt text end-to-end against StatusCodes.cs to verify referenced integers. The asymmetric danger (real duplicates leak through, transient DB3Errors get silently skipped) is exactly the kind of bug the canonical happy-path walk lens is designed to surface.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED REAL. Direct read of C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/src/LacertMCP.Server/Prompts/WorkflowPrompts.cs:291 shows the literal text `On \`DuplicateClient\` (status 18) STOP unless the operator explicitly said "skip duplicates"`. C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/src/LacertMCP.Server/Errors/StatusCodes.cs:43 defines `public const int DuplicateClient = 12;` and line 49 defines `public const int DB3Error = 18;`. The integer in the prompt is off by 6 and points at a completely different named error.

NOVELTY CONFIRMED. Grepped all four prior audit-findings*.json files for relevant keywords (DuplicateClient, "status 18", "status 12", numeric/integer mismatch). The two prior r4 findings on WorkflowPrompts.cs (P17-005, P17-006) are about *string casing* drift (clientID -> clientId, subClientID -> subClientId) — neither audited integer literals in prompt text against StatusCodes constants. r3 finding on WorkflowPrompts (line 404) is the lacerte_detail_write nested-row signature drift, also not about status integers. No prior round walked the prompt body end-to-end against StatusCodes.cs to verify referenced integers. The "status 18" parenthetical is the ONLY `(status N)` literal anywhere in src/LacertMCP.Server/Prompts (confirmed by grep), so the bug is isolated to this one site but the lens (prompt numeric literals vs StatusCodes table) is genuinely new.

MATERIALLY IMPROVES — yes, but with a nuance. The prompt's primary dispatch key is the NAME `DuplicateClient` (in backticks), not the integer; an LLM that switches on statusName will still STOP correctly on a real duplicate, and won't silently skip a DB3Error (since the LLM would see statusName=DB3Error, not the magic string `DuplicateClient`). So the "DB3Error silently skipped as duplicate" risk in the finding's impact statement is overstated — that path requires the LLM to ignore the explicit name match and key only on the parenthetical integer, which is the less natural reading. However, the bug is still material because: (1) the prompt is internally contradictory — a careful LLM that cross-references will flag uncertainty and either ask the operator or guess wrong; (2) the canonical bulk-intake prompt is REQUIREMENTS §1.3's highest-volume happy path, so any ambiguity multiplies across N rows; (3) the fix is mechanical (one digit change + drop the parenthetical) and the proposed sentinel (scrape `(status N)` patterns from prompt bodies, assert each maps to the right named StatusCodes constant) is a cheap durable guard against the same drift in any future prompt.

ACTIONABLE: 1-line edit + ~20 LOC test, sim-only, off-Windows, no SDK dependency. Identical shape to P17-005/P17-006's accepted sentinel pattern over [McpServerPrompt] bodies.

title: lacerte_client_list nameFilter is PREFIX-only on the LAST-name field (C1_2) for Individual modules — the most natural operator phrasing ('show me John', 'list everyone named Smith') silently returns 0 rows when only the first name matches
impact: Operator says 'show me John' or 'find Smith and Jones' to Claude. LLM picks nameFilter='John' (or 'Smith') and calls lacerte_client_list. For Individual modules the filter is StartsWith on C1_2 only — 'John' never matches because John is C1_1 (first name). 'Smith' matches Smith but not 'Smithson' family from a substring perspective, and never matches when the operator passes a full 'Smith, John' or a fragment like 'mith'. The LLM gets `total: 0`, tells the operator 'no clients named John' — a confidently-wrong answer to the most common phrasing the operator uses. The C# code COULD support substring + last-or-first because the in-memory store already has every row materialized.
description: ListClients at lines 730-737 picks ONE name key per module ('C1_2' for I-modules, 'C1_1' for entity modules) and does StartsWith only. The description on the tool (ClientsTools.cs:26) does say 'last-name (individual modules) or entity name', but an LLM reading that description still cannot recover from an operator's natural-language 'John' — there is no tool that searches first names. Real LLM traffic: operator '→' LLM '→' nameFilter='John' '→' empty result '→' LLM hallucinates 'you have no client named John' even though John Smith is in the roster. The other half of the gap: prefix-only means the operator's CSV-pasted 'Smith, John' (last,first format) also returns nothing because the row starts with 'Smith' not 'Smith,'. A `nameContains` / `firstNameContains` / `lastNameContains` triad — or a single `nameMatches` that scans both C1_1 and C1_2 substring — would close the gap. Cost in sim+live: trivial since the full list is already materialized and ListClients overfetches via int.MaxValue anyway.
recommendation: Add a `nameContains` parameter (case-insensitive substring) that searches BOTH C1_1 and C1_2 (and the entity-name field on non-I modules), separate from the existing `nameFilter` which keeps prefix semantics. Update the description: 'For Individual modules, nameFilter is prefix-match on C1_2 (last name only). To search first names or substrings, pass nameContains instead — scans both C1_1 (first name) and C1_2 (last name).' Same change in LacerteSessionManager.ListClients — add an `IEnumerable<string> contains` overload. Belt-and-suspenders: also emit a `hint` field on the empty-result response: 'nameFilter is last-name-prefix only; try nameContains for first-name or substring matches.' Bonus: when the filter yields zero rows BUT the unfiltered count > 0, return a hint listing the first 3 unique C1_1 + C1_2 distinct values so the LLM can disambiguate (e.g. 'Did you mean John (Jonson, Jankovic, Janus)?').
rationale: Prior rounds (P14-P17) covered the pagination contract, count-only probe, and the limit semantics — none addressed the name-filter ergonomics for natural-language LLM input. The closest priors mention overfetch and the limit clamp, not the substring-vs-prefix gap. Verified by Grep across audit-findings*.json — no result for 'nameContains', 'first name filter', 'substring match', or 'firstName.*filter'. This is the #1 mismatch between how operators talk and how the tool listens.

verdict.reasoning:
VERIFIED REAL. LacerteSessionManager.cs:730-737 confirms the exact described behavior: when `lastNameFilter` is provided, the code (a) picks a single name key per module via `var nameKey = ctx.Module == 'I' ? "C1_2" : "C1_1";` and (b) applies `StartsWith(f, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)` — prefix-only, single-field. title: Write tools document `idempotencyKey` as 'Optional' — an LLM in a retry loop (network blip, host restart mid-call, MCP transport error) regenerates the call without the key and re-executes the write; lacerte_detail_write APPENDS by default per P17-001 so each retry produces a duplicate row, and lacerte_field_write re-applies the same scalar (idempotent at the cell level for that case but invisible from the LLM's side)
impact: Real-LLM retry behavior: LLM constructs a write call, MCP host times out (Claude Desktop's stdio pipe is reliable but Cursor's MCP client has reported transient drops), LLM auto-retries by REGENERATING the tool call from the conversation context — which usually does NOT include the prior idempotencyKey because nothing in the system prompt or the tool description elevates the key as 'required for retry safety'. Result for lacerte_detail_write: a duplicate W-2 / 1099 / Dependent row appended to the live return (P17-001 confirms detail writes APPEND, replaceIndex is sim-only). Result for lacerte_field_write: the same value written twice — safe at the cell level for scalars but the LLM has no way to know if the first write succeeded vs failed, so it may infer 'this client now has email = X' wrongly. The 'Optional' wording in the description is precisely the affordance gap: an LLM treats 'Optional' as 'omit on the retry to keep the call simple', which is the opposite of safe. P17-004 added disk-persistence so the key CAN survive process restart, but that's wasted if the LLM doesn't pass a key in the first place.
description: Every write tool's idempotencyKey [Description] currently reads as 'Optional idempotency key. Same key + same payload returns the cached result for up to 24h...'. To an LLM reading the description fresh on each retry, 'Optional' means 'omit for simpler call'. The description does NOT say (a) 'STRONGLY RECOMMENDED — without this, a retry creates a duplicate row in detail writes', (b) 'Auto-suggested format: <tool>-<clientNumber>-<field>', (c) 'If you omit this and a transport error fires, you cannot safely retry — you must lacerte_detail_read to check whether the prior write landed before retrying'. The Workflow prompts DO say all this but per finding #5 those prompts often don't reach the LLM. Two complementary fixes: (i) elevate the description with a 'WARNING' prefix and a templated default; (ii) make the session manager AUTO-DERIVE a fallback key from the (tool, args) tuple when idempotencyKey is null, but ONLY for the natural-key-stable case (lacerte_field_write — same clientNumber+field+value is naturally idempotent; lacerte_detail_write CANNOT auto-derive safely because the operator might genuinely want to add a second W-2, so for that tool require the key or refuse the write).
recommendation:
Two-part fix:

(1) Rewrite every write tool's idempotencyKey [Description] to scream the consequence:
```
[Description("STRONGLY RECOMMENDED for retry safety — pass a stable string like '<tool>-<clientNumber>-<field>' so a retry after transport/timeout error replays the cached result instead of double-writing. WITHOUT this key, an MCP transport blip + LLM auto-retry will APPEND a duplicate detail row (lacerte_detail_write) or re-write the same scalar (lacerte_field_write — safe at the cell level but invisible to the LLM, which then cannot tell if its first call landed). Same key + same payload: replay (idempotent). Same key + different payload: 9102 IdempotencyConflict.")]
```

(2) Belt-and-suspenders in LacerteSessionManager.WriteField + WriteDetail: when idempotencyKey is null, log a warning to the WireLog ('write executed without idempotencyKey — retry is not safe') and stamp `idempotencyKeyAdvised: true` on the response envelope so the LLM can see it and self-correct on the NEXT call. Optionally — and this is the controversial half — add a `LACERTE_WRITE_REQUIRE_IDEMPOTENCY=1` env var that makes the session manager THROW a new synthetic code (e.g. 9018 IdempotencyKeyRequired) when null, with a remediation 'Pass idempotencyKey: "<tool>-<clientNumber>-<field>" — without this an MCP retry will double-write.' Operators who know what they're doing leave it off (back-compat); operators who got bitten once turn it on and never get bit again.

(3) Update WorkflowPrompts to surface the idempotencyKey naming convention up-front in EVERY recipe (CsvIntake already does this; ClientIntake/BulkFieldUpdate already do this — only the per-tool description needs the upgrade).
rationale: P17-004 fixed RESTART persistence of the idempotency cache — but that addresses 'the key was present, the process died, the next-process retry can still replay'. This finding is the prior step: the LLM doesn't pass a key at all. P14-005 added per-key serialization for concurrent writes. P14-013/P14-064 added TTL eviction. NONE addressed the 'optional' wording in the description or the auto-derivation fallback. title: FieldAccessDumper non-atomic shard write poisons LoadModule cache and hard-locks every write to that module
impact: If the operator kills the dumper (Ctrl-C, OS reboot, crash) mid-write of Schema/FieldAccessMap/base/{module}.json — or if antivirus pauses the file at the wrong instant — the on-disk shard is left as truncated/garbled JSON. On the next AssertWritable call for any field in that module, LoadModule.GetOrAdd's factory invokes JsonSerializer.Deserialize, which throws JsonException. Unlike LoadOverlay (which catches JsonException and caches an empty sentinel — see lines 314-333), LoadModule has NO try/catch. The thrown exception means GetOrAdd never caches the entry, so every subsequent AssertWritable for that module re-opens the file, re-parses, re-throws — surfacing to the operator as 9203 InternalServerError on every single write to that module for the rest of the process lifetime. The only recovery is restart, which kills the 24h Intuit auth ticket. The dumper's whole reason for existing was to let the operator refresh shards on a long-lived server without restart, and a crash during the refresh defeats that.
description: Program.cs:153-155 uses `Directory.CreateDirectory(...); File.WriteAllText(path, json);` with no .tmp+rename pattern. File.WriteAllText opens FileMode.Create which truncates the existing file atomically THEN streams bytes — a kill between truncate and full write leaves a half-written JSON file. The companion LoadOverlay code (FieldAccessMapLoader.cs:314-333) is explicitly defensive about exactly this failure mode ("A shipping typo in an overlay should fail open to base-map behavior, not nuke the write path"), but LoadModule was never given the same try/catch — base shards were treated as developer-curated and stable. The dumper changes that assumption: any operator-triggered shard regeneration is now a process-wide write-poison risk.
recommendation: (1) In FieldAccessDumper Program.cs:153-155, write to `path + ".tmp"` first, then `File.Delete(path); File.Move(tmp, path);` (or the same pattern used by PersistIdempotencyCacheToDisk in LacerteSessionManager.cs:2362-2369) so a kill during the write leaves the prior shard intact and an orphan .tmp the next dumper run can clean up. (2) In FieldAccessMapLoader.LoadModule (lines 261-265), wrap the Deserialize in try/catch (JsonException) and cache an empty sentinel on failure — mirror LoadOverlay's existing pattern. Adds 4 lines, prevents process-wide write-poison from a single corrupt shard, and matches the documented design intent in the LoadOverlay comment. Add a regression test: write '{ not json' to a base shard, call GetFieldAccess, assert no throw and subsequent call returns Unknown (no re-throw, no re-open).
rationale: Prior P14 finding (FieldAccessMapLoader overlay precedence + 3 of 5 AssertWritable branches untested) noted LoadOverlay needed try/catch and that was landed, but the symmetric LoadModule gap was NOT addressed and no prior round flagged the FieldAccessDumper non-atomic write as the realistic trigger. The dumper's File.WriteAllText was acceptable before P15-044 (LacerteReloadSchema MCP tool) made online shard regeneration the supported operator workflow.

- P15-034 (r2:811) covered missing/empty shards giving uniform Unknown — different failure mode (fail-open with no diagnostic), not corrupt/half-written JSON.

title: Idempotency cache persist sequence Delete-then-Move can permanently lose the file under crash or AV lock
impact: After every successful StoreIdempotent, the persist path writes tmp → Delete canonical → Move tmp → canonical. If the process is SIGKILL'd, the host OS reboots, or the antivirus briefly locks the canonical path between the Delete and the Move (Windows Defender real-time scan does this on .json writes), the canonical idempotency-cache.json is gone AND the Move never happens. The .tmp file exists but LoadIdempotencyCacheFromDisk only reads the canonical path. On the next process start the operator loses ALL idempotency keys — every prior successful WriteField/WriteDetail/CreateClient becomes invisible to the replay machinery, so a Claude-Desktop-side retry of a multi-row bulk write re-executes against the live SDK and appends a duplicate detail row per row of the batch. This is exactly the failure mode P17-004 was created to prevent; the implementation defeats its own promise.
description: Net48 lacks an atomic rename-replace primitive for the create-or-replace case (File.Replace requires destination to exist, File.Move fails if destination exists). The current code papers over that with `File.Delete; File.Move` which opens a window where the canonical path does not exist. A crash inside this window leaves the persistent cache permanently empty. The retry of a duplicate-prevention persist is also gated by the single-flight _persistingIdempotency CompareExchange — a crashed-mid-persist process can't replay the recovery because the in-memory cache is gone. Worse, the .tmp file is never cleaned up on next startup, so the operator sees a stale `idempotency-cache.json.tmp` next to the missing canonical file with no obvious recovery procedure.
recommendation: Use File.Replace when the destination exists, and File.Move only on first write: `if (File.Exists(canonical)) File.Replace(tmp, canonical, destinationBackupFileName: null); else File.Move(tmp, canonical);`. File.Replace is atomic on NTFS — the rename + delete happen as a single operation, no window where canonical is missing. Additionally, at LoadIdempotencyCacheFromDisk startup, check for a stale `idempotencyCachePath + ".tmp"` left over from a prior crash; if found AND canonical is missing, promote .tmp → canonical (the .tmp is the most recent successfully-serialized state). Add a unit test that simulates kill-between-Delete-and-Move by writing canonical, calling persist with a forced exception injected between the two ops, then loading and asserting the cache survives.
rationale: P17-004 introduced the persist machinery but the file-IO atomicity hole was not flagged by P14-P17. The risk is realistic on this exact operator profile: Lacerte runs on Windows boxes that get forced reboots from monthly Patch Tuesday, and Windows Defender's real-time scan on %APPDATA% writes is a documented intermittent .json sharing-violation source. Single-operator runtime means there's no second cache to fall back on.

Material improvement: The operator profile (Windows tax-pro running Lacerte locally with Claude Desktop / Cursor) is exactly the profile where (a) Windows Defender real-time scan intermittently locks .json writes under %APPDATA%, and (b) Patch Tuesday forced reboots are a real recurring event. title: Dry-run writes poison idempotency cache; subsequent real writes are no-ops
impact: An operator who previews a batch with dryRun=true + an idempotencyKey then runs the same batch with dryRun=false silently gets ZERO writes — every row hits the cached Success from the preview and the chokepoint never reaches the wire. The tool returns statusCode=Success for every row while the database is untouched. The same composition through lacerte_field_write_bulk (per-row key = '{prefix}-{client}-{field}') compounds the hazard across N rows.
description: BuildPayload (line 2600) fingerprints (op, table, clientNumber, field, value, subClientId, stateAbbrev) for WriteField, (clientNumber, row, replaceIndex) for WriteDetail, and (args) for CreateClient — NONE of the three include dryRun. A dryRun=true call therefore caches statusCode=Success keyed by a fingerprint that a dryRun=false call with the same parameters reproduces exactly. TryReplayIdempotent (line 1140) returns the cached Success, completely bypassing the wire call, the access-map gate, AND the WireLog.Record envelope (no log line is even emitted that the operator could grep for). The interaction is invisible to the LLM: the response shape is identical to a real successful write.
recommendation: Include dryRun in BuildPayload's args tuple at every callsite (lines 1138, 1271, 1389) so a dry-run fingerprint is distinct from a real-write fingerprint with otherwise identical args. Cheap fix; preserves the legitimate within-mode idempotency contract (two dry-runs replay, two real writes replay) while severing the cross-mode poisoning. Alternatively short-circuit StoreIdempotent when dryRun is true — the dry-run result has no semantic meaning to replay anyway since it was just rolled back.
rationale: Composition of P14 #32 (dry-run snapshot/restore) × P15-060 (idempotency cache) × P17-004 (persisted cache). Persistence amplifies it: a dry-run preview survives process restart and poisons next session's commit. Prior rounds covered each subsystem individually but never the cross-mode fingerprint elision.

title: AutoReconnect retries past wire-side mutation produce double-writes on post-write transients
impact: A live SDK call that mutates a DBF cell or appends a detail row then throws a transient HRESULT (0x800706BA RPC_S_SERVER_UNAVAILABLE during result marshaling, 0x80010108 RPC_E_DISCONNECTED after server-side commit, 0x8001010A 'busy' AFTER the inner write completed) is blindly retried 3 more times. The retry executes the WriteToDetailFile / UpdateTaxReturn / CreateClient against the SAME row again. WriteDetail appends — so a single transient on attempt 1 lands FOUR identical W-2 rows. CreateClient produces 4 duplicate clients (with whatever uniqueness the SDK enforces — the duplicate-clientId 9 IClientIDDuplicated kicks in attempts 2-4, but attempt 1 already succeeded so the FINAL exception masquerades as a duplicate-write rejection while the row IS persisted).
description: AutoReconnect.WithRetry / WithRetrySync (lines 56-141) catch any COMException whose ErrorCode is in TransientHResults and retry up to MaxRetries=3 with exponential backoff. The IsTransient gate (line 188) only inspects the HRESULT — it has no signal whether the wire-side operation completed before the COM failure. The SDK's WriteToDetailFile is append-only (per P17-001 comment line 1295), so every retry of a successful-but-marshal-failed write IS a duplicate append. WriteField/CreateClient have similar at-most-once semantics required by the SDK that AutoReconnect cannot guarantee. Idempotency cache doesn't help: TryReplayIdempotent runs BEFORE the retry loop (line 1140), so the retry loop and the cache are at different scopes — the cache only sees the FINAL outcome of all 4 attempts.
recommendation: Either (a) restrict transient retries to PRE-CALL HRESULTs only (RPC_S_SERVER_UNAVAILABLE 0x800706BA before the call dispatched is safe; AFTER is not, but the bridge can't distinguish) and drop 0x80010108/0x8001010A entirely since they're observed AFTER the server has the call; or (b) move the idempotency replay INSIDE the retry loop so each attempt consults the cache (after the FIRST attempt succeeds in mutating the DB, store its result under a wire-attempt sub-key so attempts 2+ short-circuit). Both are non-trivial; the simplest mitigation is documenting in DECISIONS.md that AutoReconnect is unsafe for detail-row APPEND and gating WriteDetail with a wire-side 'I already wrote this' fingerprint check via ReadDetail after a transient retry.
rationale: Composition of P15-014 (AutoReconnect) × P15-060 (idempotency cache scope) × P17-001 (live WriteDetail append-only). Prior rounds verified the retry whitelist HRESULTs and the cache TTL, but never the gap between the SDK wire mutation and the cache lookup.

The IsTransient gate (line 188-217) inspects ONLY the HRESULT — it has no signal whether the wire-side mutation completed before the COM/RPC failure surfaced.

2. AutoReconnect.WithRetry (lines 56-104) retries up to MaxRetries=3 unconditionally on any whitelisted HRESULT — no read-after-write fingerprint check, no IsIdempotentOp gate, no transient-class subdivision (pre-dispatch vs post-dispatch).

The deeper fix (split TransientHResults into pre/post-dispatch tiers — retry only RPC_S_SERVER_UNAVAILABLE 0x800706BA when it's a connection-refused-from-the-start signal — and inject a pre-call probe to disambiguate) is harder but the finding correctly flags it as non-trivial.

CONFIDENCE: high. Code paths verified directly; HRESULT semantics are documented Microsoft COM/RPC; novelty confirmed by exhaustive prior-round grep; impact is concrete and in the operator's documented workflow.

title: ExecuteWithIdempotencyLock's GetOrAdd → WaitAsync window can ObjectDisposedException when EvictIdempotencyEntry concurrently disposes the semaphore
impact: Under the documented 'idempotency cap reached + concurrent same-key call' scenario, thread A calls GetOrAdd → gets sem instance X → schedules WaitAsync. Thread B (eviction sweep crossing the 10k cap) executes EvictIdempotencyEntry on that same key, observes CurrentCount==1, atomically KVP-removes, then calls sem.Dispose() BEFORE thread A reaches sem.WaitAsync(). Thread A then throws ObjectDisposedException, which surfaces to the operator as a raw InternalServerError instead of either a clean retry or the intended idempotency behavior. The P15-012/P15-055 comment claims 'worst case is one extra execution of the body' but that's only true if the GetOrAdd happens AFTER the dispose — the window where GetOrAdd already returned X but WaitAsync hasn't fired yet is not protected.
description: Line 1938: `var sem = _idempotencyLocks.GetOrAdd(key, _ => new SemaphoreSlim(1, 1));` returns a reference. Line 1939: `await sem.WaitAsync()`. Between these two lines the evictor at 1969-1972 can run: the KVP-remove succeeds (the dict still holds the matching pair), then `sem.Dispose()` fires. The atomic KVP-remove protects against a NEW concurrent GetOrAdd swapping in a fresh sem (which would mismatch the pair and skip removal), but it does NOT protect a pre-existing reference held by thread A that hasn't yet entered the wait. The CurrentCount==1 check at line 1964 is correct at the instant it's read but not preserved through the dispose — and even if held, WaitAsync.Dispose() throws.
recommendation: Three options, increasing strength: (a) wrap WaitAsync in try/catch (ObjectDisposedException) and retry the whole ExecuteWithIdempotencyLock — semantically equivalent to 'lost the lock, re-acquire'; (b) skip dispose entirely — let the GC collect orphaned SemaphoreSlim instances (small leak but eliminates the race); (c) use a refcount + dispose-when-zero pattern (heavier; matches the existing CurrentCount intuition but actually correct). For a single-operator tax-pro use case where eviction is rare, option (a) is the lowest-risk patch. Add a regression test that 1) seeds the cache to (cap-1) entries, 2) launches 32 parallel calls with the SAME key while a second thread force-runs the eviction sweep — without the fix, ObjectDisposedException eventually surfaces.
rationale: The P15-012/P15-055 self-comment explicitly flags 'worst case is one extra execution of the body' as the worst case — proving the team analyzed the new-GetOrAdd-after-dispose direction but missed the pre-existing-reference direction. The mitigation is small (~5 lines) and the test cost is contained.

title: field_write_bulk prompt Step 2 enumerates ReadOnly/Hidden/NotExposed/NotSupported in the STOP list but omits Unknown — the v1 default access state
impact: The bulk-write prompt walks the operator through a high-risk N-row write across an arbitrary field. Step 2 tells the LLM to STOP if the field is `ReadOnly / Hidden / NotExposed / NotSupported` — but does NOT mention Unknown (the default state for the empty v1 shards) AND does not mention 'field absent from the map response entirely'. MetadataTools.LacerteFieldAccessMap (MetadataTools.cs:109) actively filters out Unknown entries from the response, so a v1-shard field appears NOT in the map at all. An LLM literally reading the prompt's STOP list might conclude 'field is not on the STOP list, therefore safe to bulk-write' — and proceed to fire 500 writes through the chokepoint, each of which will get rejected with synthetic 9012 UnknownFieldAccess (AssertWritable). The operator sees a 500-row failure envelope when a one-line prompt warning would have prevented the round-trip. Compare to lacerte_csv_intake Step 2 (line 278) which DOES mention Unknown — the two prompts disagree.
description: WorkflowPrompts.cs:208-209 (BulkFieldUpdate Step 2) reads: `Confirm {fieldLabel} is ReadWrite. If ReadOnly / Hidden / NotExposed / NotSupported, STOP and tell the operator the field can't be bulk-updated.` This list omits FieldAccess.Unknown (the default for any field not present in the shard JSON) AND does not address 'field absent from lacerte_field_access_map response entirely' — which is the actual v1 state for everything except C{t}_0. The CSV intake prompt (line 278) handles this correctly: `If Unknown / ReadOnly / Hidden, STOP`. The two prompts are inconsistent. Worse, the bulk tool defaults to a 500-entry cap (FieldWriteBulkTools.cs:62) — a single LLM mistake here means 500 wasted SDK round-trips.
recommendation: Edit WorkflowPrompts.cs:208-209 to: `Confirm {fieldLabel} appears in the response AND its access is ReadWrite. If Unknown / absent / ReadOnly / Hidden / NotExposed / NotSupported, STOP and tell the operator the field can't be bulk-updated. (v1 shards are empty by design — most fields will be absent. Until Todo.md F5 ships full introspection, only C{t}_0 is in the map for every module/table; everything else returns Unknown.)`. Optional follow-up: have LacerteFieldAccessMap surface a `requestedField` parameter so the LLM can do a single targeted probe and get a definitive {access: 'Unknown'} response instead of inferring absence from a filtered enumeration — kills the prompt-text inconsistency at the tool boundary.
rationale: P14/P15/P16 prompt findings focused on tool names (P16-052 alignment), envelope keys (P16-024 rows canonicalization), and parameter renames. The Unknown-vs-empty-shard interaction with the bulk-write STOP gate is a prompt-correctness issue specifically — and the CSV vs Bulk inconsistency (CSV does list Unknown, Bulk doesn't) is a smoking-gun no prior cross-prompt walk caught.

If `ReadOnly` / `Hidden` / `NotExposed` / `NotSupported`, STOP..." — Unknown is missing. WorkflowPrompts.cs:278 (CsvIntake Step 2) reads: "If `Unknown` / `ReadOnly` / `Hidden`, STOP..." — Unknown is present. MetadataTools.cs:109 confirms the filter: `if (access == FieldAccess.Unknown && f != universal) continue;` — Unknown entries are dropped from the returned `fields` dict entirely. Combined with v1's empty shards (per docstring at line 104-108: "the empty shards return Unknown for every probe except the universal C{t}_0 rule"), the operational reality is: in v1, every field except `C{t}_0` is ABSENT from the response, not labeled Unknown. So an LLM literally reading BulkFieldUpdate Step 2's STOP list would see "field not in {ReadOnly, Hidden, NotExposed, NotSupported}" and proceed — firing N writes that all reject with 9012 UnknownFieldAccess at the AssertWritable chokepoint.

NOVELTY: Searched all 4 prior round JSONs for: BulkFieldUpdate, WorkflowPrompts, STOP list, Unknown.*absent, inconsistent prompt. Prior WorkflowPrompts findings cover: README documentation of prompts (P14:316), parameter naming alignment (P15-038, P16-080), prompt test coverage (P15:1172), tool-name rename (P16-052), and ALL-CAPS rebind to clientId/emailId (P17-103 at r4:103). NONE of these address: (a) the Unknown-omission in BulkFieldUpdate's STOP list, (b) the CsvIntake-vs-BulkFieldUpdate inconsistency, or (c) the LacerteFieldAccessMap-filters-Unknown interaction with that STOP gate. The cross-prompt walk + access-map response-shape interaction is the smoking-gun novelty.

Fix is a single sentence in the prompt template — cheapest possible change, sim-testable via existing WorkflowPromptsTests, and aligns the two prompts' contracts.

CONFIDENCE high: code reads verified verbatim at all 3 cited line locations, inconsistency is intra-file (one prompt away from the gap), and the v1-shard semantics are documented in code comments at MetadataTools.cs:97-109 making the consequence unambiguous.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Edit WorkflowPrompts.cs:209 (Step 2 of BulkFieldUpdate). Refined text that handles the absent-from-response case AND mirrors the CsvIntake STOP list:

  "Call `lacerte_field_access_map` with the active module + table. The response's `fields` dict only contains entries for fields whose access is NOT `Unknown` (the loader filters Unknown to reduce noise). Confirm `{fieldLabel}` appears in `fields` AND its value is exactly `ReadWrite`. STOP if any of: field is absent from `fields` / access is `Unknown` / `ReadOnly` / `Hidden` / `NotExposed` / `NotSupported`. (NOTE: until Todo.md F5 lands full shard introspection, only `C{table}_0` is cataloged ReadWrite for every module — every other field on a v1 module returns Unknown and will be absent from the response. If you don't see `{fieldLabel}` listed, that's the STOP signal — do NOT proceed and bulk-write {N} entries that the chokepoint will reject with 9012 UnknownFieldAccess.)"

1. Mirror the same wording in CsvIntake Step 2 (line 278) for parity — current "If `Unknown` / `ReadOnly` / `Hidden`, STOP" omits NotExposed/NotSupported and the absent-from-response case.
2. Add a regression test in WorkflowPromptsTests.cs that asserts both prompt texts contain the same canonical STOP-list tokens — locks the two prompts together so future edits to one don't drift.
3. (Optional, larger) Add a `requestedField` parameter to LacerteFieldAccessMap so a caller can do a targeted probe and get an explicit `{access: "Unknown"}` row back instead of inferring absence — kills the prompt-text inconsistency at the tool boundary. Tracked as a Todo.md follow-up, not blocking.

title: lacerte_session_status carries no actionable hint when context is null — the LLM must call ANY read tool, eat a 9009 ContextNotSet error, parse its remediation, and only THEN learn the recovery path; preemptive guidance lives in the error catalog but not in the status response
line: 43-86 (LacerteSessionStatus — emits context: null with no nextSteps hint)
impact: Cold-start LLM flow: operator says 'show me my clients'. LLM calls lacerte_session_status (smart move — checking state first). Response has `context: null`. There is NO field telling the LLM what to do next — no `nextSteps`, no `hint`, no `requiredTools` array. The LLM either (a) guesses correctly that it should call lacerte_set_context (and either knows or guesses the right datapath/year/module), or (b) proceeds straight to lacerte_client_list which throws 9009 ContextNotSet, whose remediation it reads, and finally takes the right recovery action. Path (b) burns a round-trip AND an error envelope per session start. The remediation text for 9009 (SyntheticStatusCodes.cs:236) is actually well-written and gives the canonical path 'list_datapaths → list_modules → set_context' — it should be EMITTED PREEMPTIVELY on the session-status response whenever context is null, not buried as a reactive error.
description: The session status response shape (SessionTools.cs:54-85) emits `mode, isRegistered, registeredAt, expiresAt, minutesUntilExpiry, context, appName, appId, debugWireEnabled, wireLogPath` — no field tells the LLM 'what to do next'. The 9009 ContextNotSet remediation already says: 'First call lacerte_list_datapaths..., then lacerte_list_modules..., then lacerte_set_context(dataPath, taxYear, module). In simulation mode the canonical seeded paths are C:\Lacerte\20Tax\IData...' — every byte of that text is what the LLM needs at session_status time when context is null, but it only arrives wrapped in an error envelope from a different tool call. Same problem for isRegistered=false: the LLM has to call any tool, eat NotSignedIn (203), and only then learn to ask the operator to run `lacerte-mcp register`. A `nextSteps: [string]` array on session_status — populated based on current gaps — would short-circuit the entire error-as-discovery loop. P16-066 already added debugWireEnabled+wireLogPath for log-grep discovery; this is the same pattern applied to session bootstrap.
recommendation: Add a `nextSteps` array (or `bootstrapHint` string) to the LacerteSessionStatus response. Build it deterministically: (1) if !isRegistered → push 'Run `lacerte-mcp register` on the Lacerte box to grant 24h auth.'; (2) if context == null → push 'No active context. Call lacerte_list_datapaths to discover available (path, taxYear, module) triples, then lacerte_set_context(dataPath, taxYear, module). In simulation mode the seeded paths are C:\\Lacerte\\20Tax\\IData (TY20 individual), C:\\Lacerte\\24Tax\\IData (TY24 individual), C:\\Lacerte\\24Tax\\CData (TY24 corp), C:\\Lacerte\\24Tax\\PData (TY24 partnership).'; (3) if context != null AND expiresAt within 10 minutes → push 'Auth ticket expires soon — run `lacerte-mcp login` to refresh BEFORE the next write.'; (4) if context.readOnly → push 'Active context is readOnly — every write tool will throw 9001 FieldIsReadOnly until you re-call lacerte_set_context with readOnly:false.'. Empty array on the happy path is fine. Single source of truth: extract the message texts from SyntheticStatusCodes.StatusTable so a future remediation edit auto-propagates. Adds <100 bytes when populated, zero when empty, and short-circuits an entire round-trip-and-error class.
rationale: P16-081 added a `hint` to client_read for the not-found case. P16-066 added debugWireEnabled/wireLogPath to session_status for log discovery. P16-024 added consistent `rows` keys. NONE made session_status carry preemptive nextSteps for cold-start. The error-catalog remediation (9009, 203, 9007) is well-written; this finding just routes it to the right surface — the snapshot the LLM ALREADY calls first.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified by reading SessionTools.cs:42-86, SessionStatusSnapshot.cs (all 56 lines), and SyntheticStatusCodes.cs:232-236. The current LacerteSessionStatus tool emits {mode, isRegistered, registeredAt, expiresAt, minutesUntilExpiry, context, appName, appId, debugWireEnabled, wireLogPath} — confirmed NO nextSteps/hint/bootstrap field exists. Grep across the entire repo for `nextSteps|bootstrapHint|nextStep|next_step` returned zero matches in source code (no implementation, no tests).

Novelty check against prior 4 rounds: closest neighbors found are (a) P16-041 (audit-findings-r3.json:1003-1025) which added a `Next:` hint to the CLI `lacerte-mcp status` command — a different surface (CLI, not MCP tool); (b) P16-042 (audit-findings-r3.json:1027-1049) which tightened the ContextNotSet REACTIVE error remediation and added sim-mode seed paths — confirmed shipped via SyntheticStatusCodes.cs:236; (c) P16-066 which added debugWireEnabled/wireLogPath to the same session_status snapshot — proves the pattern of adding affordance fields to the snapshot is precedented but was scoped narrowly to log-grep discovery. NO prior task added preemptive bootstrap guidance to the MCP `lacerte_session_status` tool response itself.

The finding's central claim is exactly right: P16-042 wrote excellent canonical-path text but routed it only through the reactive error envelope on a different tool. An LLM calling session_status as its first move (smart, defensive) gets `context: null` with no hint, then must call a read tool, eat the 9009 envelope, and only then learn the recovery path. Surfacing the SAME text proactively on the snapshot short-circuits a round-trip plus an error per cold-start session.

Material improvement: yes — measurable: one fewer tool-call + one fewer error envelope on every fresh session start, with zero shape impact on the happy path (empty array). The author's #4 (readOnly hint) is the weakest of the four conditions because readOnly=true is usually intentional, but #1 (not registered), #2 (context null), and #3 (expiry within 10 min) are clear wins. Single-source-of-truth idea — reuse SyntheticStatusCodes.StatusTable[ContextNotSet/LoginExpired/AppNotRegistered].Remediation strings — is a clean tightening that avoids the duplicated-string-drift bug class that R2/R3 already chased in other places.

Not a duplicate, actionable in-session (pure additive C# in SessionStatusSnapshot + SessionTools + 4 SessionToolsTests cases), no breaking changes, and aligned with the P16-066 precedent of "surface what the next-step error would tell you, before the error fires."
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Add a `nextSteps` field (List<string> or string[]) to SessionStatusSnapshot and emit it on the LacerteSessionStatus MCP tool response. Build deterministically and DRY against the existing error catalog so future copy-edits to SyntheticStatusCodes.StatusTable auto-propagate:

1. SessionStatusSnapshot.cs — append `IReadOnlyList<string> NextSteps = null` (default empty list, never null on the wire).

2. LacerteSessionManager.SessionStatus() — populate NextSteps in priority order, pulling the message text from `SyntheticStatusCodes.StatusTable[code].Remediation` so there is ONE source of truth:
   - If `!IsRegistered`: append StatusTable[AppNotRegistered].Remediation (already says "Run `lacerte-mcp register`...").
   - Else if `Context == null`: append StatusTable[ContextNotSet].Remediation (already lists the canonical bootstrap path with seeded sim paths after P16-042).
   - Else if `MinutesUntilExpiry < 10`: append StatusTable[LoginExpired].Remediation prefixed with "Auth ticket expires in {N} min — preempt: ".
   - Skip the readOnly hint from the original finding — readOnly=true is operator-intentional, not a gap.

3. SessionTools.cs:54-85 — emit `nextSteps = s.NextSteps` after wireLogPath. Always present (empty array on happy path keeps the shape stable).

4. SessionToolsTests — add cases: (a) unregistered → nextSteps contains "lacerte-mcp register"; (b) registered but no context → nextSteps contains "lacerte_list_datapaths" and "C:\Lacerte\24Tax\IData"; (c) auth within 10 min of expiry → nextSteps contains "lacerte-mcp login"; (d) fully registered + context set + not near expiry → nextSteps is empty array.

5. NamingConventionsTests — assert `nextSteps` camelCase and is `string[]` not `object`, matching the existing array-shape contract.

Key design points: (i) Single source of truth — the remediation strings live ONLY in StatusTable so the next remediation edit (e.g. when the seeded paths shift) automatically reflects in session_status without a second edit site. (ii) Additive on the wire — empty array on the happy path; no breaking change. (iii) Reuses the P16-066 precedent (same snapshot surface, same "preempt the error" intent). (iv) Skip the JSON-shape change for `readOnly` since that state is user-intentional. (v) Bonus: update WorkflowPrompts intake prompt to mention that `lacerte_session_status` now self-describes its own next step — reinforces the "call status first" pattern that ContextNotSet alone cannot teach.
